# the library's contract: arm environment lines (gates: false → LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false)
# land in ARM_ENV_FILE; write_sandbox_grimoire resolves sprint_plan from LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE
export ARM_ENV_FILE="$META/arm-env"; : > "$ARM_ENV_FILE"
export LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE="$SUITE_FILE"

lib_call() {  # lib_call <fn> <args…> — stdout appended to the evidence file; non-zero → infra
  local fn="$1" out rc=0; shift
  out="$("$fn" "$@" 2>>"$MOUNT_LOG")" || rc=$?
  [[ -n "$out" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$out" >> "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE"
  [[ $rc -eq 0 ]] || infra "$fn exited $rc (see meta/mount.log)"
  LIB_OUT="$out"
}

LIB_OUT=""
lib_call resolve_arm_toggles "$ARM" "$SUITE_FILE"
TOGGLES="$(printf '%s\n' "$LIB_OUT" | sed -n '/^[[:space:]]*[{]/,$p')"
if [[ -z "$TOGGLES" ]] || ! jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$TOGGLES"; then
  infra "resolve_arm_toggles printed no toggles object"
fi
TOGGLES="$(jq -c '.' <<<"$TOGGLES")"
# the toggles object is evidence, not a key=value line: drop it from the evidence file
grep -E '^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+=' "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE" > "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE.tmp" || true
mv "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE.tmp" "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE"
PLAN_JSON="$(plan_phases "$TOGGLES")"
LOA_MOUNT=true; [[ "$(jq -r '.loa_mount' <<<"$TOGGLES")" == false ]] && LOA_MOUNT=false
SINGLE_SESSION=false; [[ "$(jq -r '.context_resets' <<<"$TOGGLES")" == false ]] && SINGLE_SESSION=true
GATES_OFF=false; [[ "$(jq -r '.gates' <<<"$TOGGLES")" == false ]] && GATES_OFF=true
FLATLINE=on; [[ "$(jq -r '.flatline' <<<"$TOGGLES")" == false ]] && FLATLINE=off

# --- fingerprint / image ---------------------------------------------------------
if [[ "$EXECUTOR" == host ]]; then
  command -v "$CLAUDE_BIN" >/dev/null 2>&1 || [[ -x "$CLAUDE_BIN" ]] || infra "claude CLI not found: $CLAUDE_BIN"
fi
FINGERPRINT="$("$SCRIPT_DIR/fingerprint.sh" --source-tree "$SOURCE_TREE" --claude-bin "$CLAUDE_BIN" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
if [[ "$EXECUTOR" == container ]]; then
  command -v "$DOCKER_BIN" >/dev/null 2>&1 || [[ -x "$DOCKER_BIN" ]] || infra "docker CLI not found: $DOCKER_BIN"
  IMAGE_DIGEST="$("$DOCKER_BIN" image inspect --format '{{if .RepoDigests}}{{index .RepoDigests 0}}{{else}}{{.Id}}{{end}}' "$IMAGE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  [[ -n "$IMAGE_DIGEST" ]] || infra "container image not found: $IMAGE"
else
  IMAGE_DIGEST="$FINGERPRINT"
fi

# --- materialisation (D-4.5) -------------------------------------------------------
resolve_rel() {  # resolve_rel <relpath> → first existing dir among the candidate roots
  local rel="$1" c
  if [[ "$rel" == /* ]]; then [[ -d "$rel" ]] && { printf '%s' "$rel"; return 0; }; return 1; fi
  for c in "$TASK_DIR/$rel" "$SUITE_ROOT/$rel" "$REPO_ROOT/$rel" "$REPO_ROOT/evals/fixtures/$rel" "$SOURCE_TREE/evals/fixtures/$rel"; do
    [[ -d "$c" ]] && { (cd "$c" && pwd); return 0; }
  done
  return 1
}
sgit() {  # git on the sandbox repo, isolated from the operator's git config
  env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$META" GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 LC_ALL=C \
    git -C "$WS" "$@"
}

if [[ "$KIND" == build ]]; then
  fx_rel="$(jq -r '.fixture // ""' <<<"$TASK_JSON")"
  [[ -n "$fx_rel" ]] || infra "build task has no fixture"
  FIXTURE_DIR="$(resolve_rel "$fx_rel")" || infra "fixture not found: $fx_rel"
  case "/$FIXTURE_DIR/" in */hidden/*) infra "fixture resolves inside a hidden directory: $fx_rel" ;; esac
  lib_call check_fixture_path_rule "$FIXTURE_DIR"
  cp -a "$FIXTURE_DIR/." "$WS/"
else
  fx_rel="$(jq -r '.review_catch.fixture // .fixture // ""' <<<"$TASK_JSON")"
  [[ -n "$fx_rel" ]] || infra "review-catch task has no review_catch.fixture"
  FIXTURE_DIR="$(resolve_rel "$fx_rel")" || infra "review-catch fixture not found: $fx_rel"
  mkdir -p "$WS/pr"
  for p in base head head.diff PR.md REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md; do
    [[ -e "$FIXTURE_DIR/$p" ]] && cp -a "$FIXTURE_DIR/$p" "$WS/pr/"
  done
  [[ -f "$WS/pr/head.diff" ]] || infra "review-catch fixture has no head.diff: $fx_rel"
fi

# base commit: the fixture tree only; the mount paths are excluded so the gates'
# diff (base..HEAD) and the snapshots carry the agent's work, not the harness.
sgit init -q
sgit config user.name eval
sgit config user.email eval@loa
sgit config commit.gpgsign false
{
  printf '%s\n' '/.claude/' '/CLAUDE.md' '/.loa.config.yaml' '/grimoires/' '/.run/' '/.beads/' '/.eval/'
} >> "$WS/.git/info/exclude"
sgit add -A
sgit commit -q --allow-empty -m base
BASE_COMMIT="$(sgit rev-parse HEAD)"
printf 'base_commit=%s\n' "$BASE_COMMIT" >> "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE"

if [[ "$LOA_MOUNT" == true ]]; then
  lib_call mount_prompt_surface "$WS" "$SOURCE_TREE" -
fi
lib_call apply_arm_toggles "$WS" "$TOGGLES" "$ARM"
if [[ "$LOA_MOUNT" == true ]]; then
  lib_call write_sandbox_grimoire "$WS" "$TASK_YAML" "$ARM" "$SPRINT"
  lib_call init_sandbox_beads "$WS" "$(jq -r '.title // .id' <<<"$TASK_JSON")"
  mkdir -p "$WS/.run"
  [[ -e "$WS/.run/zone-guard-authorization.json" ]] && infra "sandbox carries .run/zone-guard-authorization.json"
  lib_call regen_sandbox_manifest "$WS"
  grep -q '^manifest_sha256=' "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE" || infra "regen_sandbox_manifest printed no manifest_sha256"
else
  [[ -e "$WS/.claude" || -e "$WS/CLAUDE.md" ]] && infra "loa_mount: false but the sandbox has .claude/ or CLAUDE.md"
  printf 'loa_mount=none\n' >> "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE"
fi
mkdir -p "$WS/.eval/tmp" "$WS/.eval/gh-empty"
: > "$WS/.eval/model-invoke.jsonl"
: > "$WS/.eval/cost-ledger.jsonl"

run_phase() {  # run_phase <name> <label>
  local name="$1" label="$2" model turns tsec prompt_file events errf argv_file
  local -a cargv envkv full
  model="$(phase_model "$name")"
  turns="$(phase_cap "$name" max_turns)"
  tsec="$(phase_timeout_s "$name")"
  prompt_file="$META/prompt-$label.md"
  events="$TRANS/events-$label.jsonl"; errf="$TRANS/stderr-$label.log"
  argv_file="$META/phase-$label.argv.json"
  build_prompt "$name" "$prompt_file"
  local why; why="$(leak_scan "$prompt_file")" || infra "phase prompt $label leaks $why"

  local resume=""
  if [[ "$SINGLE_SESSION" == true && -n "$IMPL_SESSION" ]]; then
    case "$name" in PLAN|IMPLEMENT|FIX) resume="$IMPL_SESSION" ;; esac
  fi
  local cbin="$CLAUDE_BIN"; [[ "$EXECUTOR" == container ]] && cbin="${LOA_EVAL_CONTAINER_CLAUDE_BIN:-claude}"
  cargv=("$cbin" -p "$(cat "$prompt_file")" --output-format stream-json --verbose --model "$model"
         --permission-mode bypassPermissions --dangerously-skip-permissions --setting-sources project
         --tools "$TOOLS" --max-turns "$turns")
  [[ -n "$EFFORT_FLAG" ]] && cargv+=(--effort "$EFFORT_FLAG")
  [[ -n "$resume" ]] && cargv+=(--resume "$resume")

  local ev_ws="$WS" home_v="$HOME" path_v="$PATH"
  if [[ "$EXECUTOR" == container ]]; then
    ev_ws="/workspace"; home_v="/home/evaluser"; path_v="/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"
  fi
  envkv=("PATH=$path_v" "HOME=$home_v" "LANG=${LANG:-C.UTF-8}" "LC_ALL=$LC_ALL" "TERM=${TERM:-dumb}"
         "TMPDIR=$ev_ws/.eval/tmp" "CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=${CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK:-1}")
  local pk
  for pk in $PASS_KEYS; do
    if [[ -n "${!pk:-}" ]]; then envkv+=("$pk=${!pk}"); fi
  done
  envkv+=("CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=$model"
          "LOA_MODELINV_LOG_PATH=$ev_ws/.eval/model-invoke.jsonl"
          "LOA_COST_LEDGER_PATH=$ev_ws/.eval/cost-ledger.jsonl"
          "GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null" "GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1" "GH_CONFIG_DIR=$ev_ws/.eval/gh-empty")
  local kv_arm have_enforce=false
  while IFS= read -r kv_arm; do
    [[ "$kv_arm" =~ ^LOA_[A-Z0-9_]+= ]] || continue    # the arm's own variables only (never PATH, HOME, keys)
    envkv+=("$kv_arm"); [[ "$kv_arm" == LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=* ]] && have_enforce=true
  done < <(LC_ALL=C sort -u "$ARM_ENV_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ "$GATES_OFF" == true && "$have_enforce" == false ]] && envkv+=("LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false")

  local cname="" keys="" kv k
  for kv in "${envkv[@]}"; do keys="$keys${keys:+,}${kv%%=*}"; done
  if [[ "$EXECUTOR" == container ]]; then
    cname="loa-abl-$(printf '%s-%s' "$RUN_ID" "$label" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9_.-' '-' | cut -c1-100)"
    # the docker client keeps only what it needs plus the secrets it forwards by name
    local hostkeys="PATH,HOME,DOCKER_HOST,DOCKER_CONFIG,XDG_RUNTIME_DIR"
    for k in $SECRET_KEYS; do if [[ -n "${!k:-}" ]]; then hostkeys="$hostkeys,$k"; fi; done
    full=(python3 -I -c "$ENV_SHIM" "$hostkeys"
          "$DOCKER_BIN" run --rm --name "$cname" --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)"
          --network bridge --read-only --tmpfs /tmp:rw,size=1g
          --pids-limit 512 --memory 4g --cpus 2
          -v "$WS:/workspace:rw"
          -v "$HOME_DIR:/home/evaluser:rw"
          -w /workspace)
    for kv in "${envkv[@]}"; do
      k="${kv%%=*}"
      if [[ "$SECRET_KEYS" == *" $k "* ]]; then full+=(-e "$k"); else full+=(-e "$kv"); fi
    done
    full+=("$IMAGE" python3 -I -c "$ENV_SHIM" "$keys" timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=15 "$tsec" "${cargv[@]}")
  else
    full=(python3 -I -c "$ENV_SHIM" "$keys" timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=15 "$tsec" "${cargv[@]}")
  fi

  # argv + environment capture (took-effect.sh reads it; the grader never does)
  jq -n --arg label "$label" --arg name "$name" --arg executor "$EXECUTOR" --arg cwd "$ev_ws" \
    --arg resume "$resume" --argjson tsec "$tsec" \
    --argjson argv "$(printf '%s\0' "${cargv[@]}" | jq -Rs 'split("\u0000") | .[:-1]')" \
    --argjson env "$(printf '%s\0' "${envkv[@]}" | jq -Rs --arg secret "$SECRET_KEYS" 'split("\u0000") | .[:-1]
        | map(capture("^(?<k>[^=]+)=(?<v>.*)$"; "s")) | map(.k as $k | {($k): (if ($secret | contains(" " + $k + " ")) then "<set>" else .v end)}) | add')" \
    --argjson launcher "$(printf '%s\0' "${full[@]}" | jq -Rs 'split("\u0000") | .[:-1]')" \
    '{label: $label, name: $name, executor: $executor, cwd: $cwd, timeout_s: $tsec,
      resume: (if $resume == "" then null else $resume end), argv: $argv, env: $env,
      launcher_argv: $launcher, container: ($executor == "container")}' > "$argv_file"

  local ledger_before=0 started_iso start_s end_s rc=0 prices killed=0 cap_turn=0 est="0 0 0" budget
  ledger_before="$(wc -l < "$WS/.eval/cost-ledger.jsonl" | tr -d ' ')"
  local minv_before minv_after
  minv_before="$(wc -l < "$WS/.eval/model-invoke.jsonl" | tr -d ' ')"
  started_iso="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
  start_s="$(now_ms)"
  prices="$(price_for "$model")"
  budget=$(( CAP_MICRO - SPENT_MICRO ))
  CUR_LABEL="$label" CUR_CONTAINER="$cname"

# suite-lib.bash — fixture-suite builders for validate-suite.bats and freeze.bats
# (cycle-130 Sprint 258 Task 1.11). Sourced by the bats files; the templates are
# the two committed smoke tasks, so the fixtures follow the real schema.
#
#   make_task <root> <group> <id> <type>   copy a smoke task to <root>/<group>/<id>
#                                          as <type> (build types from smoke-build-01,
#                                          review-catch from smoke-review-01)
#   make_full_suite <root>                 four tasks of each type under tasks/

SMOKE_ROOT="${SMOKE_ROOT:-$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke}"

make_task() {
  local root="$1" group="$2" id="$3" type="$4" src
  case "$type" in review-catch) src="$SMOKE_ROOT/smoke-review-01" ;; *) src="$SMOKE_ROOT/smoke-build-01" ;; esac
  mkdir -p "$root/$group"
  cp -a "$src" "$root/$group/$id"
  local ty="$root/$group/$id/task.yaml"
  ID="$id" TY="$type" yq -i '.id = strenv(ID) | .type = strenv(TY)' "$ty"
  if [[ "$type" != "review-catch" ]]; then
    FX="$group/$id/fixture" yq -i '.fixture = strenv(FX)' "$ty"
  fi
  if [[ "$type" == "refactor" ]]; then
    printf 'def test_structure():\n    assert True\n' > "$root/$group/$id/hidden/tests/test_structure_check.py"
    yq -i '.structural_check = "hidden/tests/test_structure_check.py"' "$ty"
  fi
}

make_full_suite() {
  local root="$1" ty i
  for ty in feature-build bug-fix refactor review-catch; do
    for i in 1 2 3 4; do make_task "$root" tasks "$ty-0$i" "$ty"; done
  done
}

content.text:
I found 13 defects in the scoped files. Several I reproduced in a scratch copy under `/tmp/s` (with a stub `compat-lib.sh`); the rest I confirmed by reading the code. They are ranked by severity, and nothing under `/workspace/pr` was modified.

1. `head/.claude/scripts/preflight.sh:190` — The new count comes from `git ls-files -- .claude`, which reads the git index, not the files on disk.
   - **Detection is lost:** deleting a tracked System Zone file, or adding a stray file, no longer changes the count, so the "modified outside the update process" check can no longer catch those changes. Reproduced: with one tracked file deleted and an untracked file added, the count stayed at 2.
   - **New false mismatches:** a downstream that commits `.claude/` but whose manifest came from the legacy `find`-based generators (mount-loa.sh / update.sh, per gen-checksums.sh:6-10) lists files git doesn't track. Its count now differs from the manifest, which is `exit 1` under `strict`.
   - **Smaller mismatch:** it also counts tracked paths that gen-checksums.sh:96 skips (gitlinks, dangling symlinks, symlinks to directories).

2. `head/tools/check-manifest-paths.sh:80` — `git ls-files` runs without `-z`, so git escapes non-ASCII paths (`".claude/caf\303\251.sh"`), while the jq keys at line 81 are raw UTF-8. A correct manifest from gen-checksums.sh (which uses `-z`) fails the CI gate. Reproduced: `.claude/café.sh` was reported as untracked `[other]`, exit 1.

3. `head/tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh:133` — The overlay only walks `ls-files --cached --others`. A file removed with `git rm`, or the old path of a `git mv`, is no longer in the index, so it stays in the upstream clone. The header (line 13) promises deletions are applied, so `--worktree` mounts a tree that still contains removed files. Also, with `--ref` other than HEAD, every work-tree file is copied over REF, so the result is not "REF plus uncommitted state" as documented.

4. `head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:144-154` — In skill mode, the `cp -a` of the skill dir (144), the `cp` of `CLAUDE.loa.md` (146), the `cp -a` of rules (150) and the config copy (154) are not checked (likewise 132-133 in tree mode). Callers invoke the function as `... || exit 2` (execute-agent) or inside `$(...) || rc=$?` (pipeline-run), and both turn off `set -e` inside the function. A failed copy therefore still returns 0, and the arm runs with an incomplete prompt surface. Base execute-agent ran these copies at top level, where `set -e` aborted, so this breaks the header's "WITHOUT behaviour change" claim.

5. `head/.claude/scripts/check-loa.sh:75` — In a submodule mount, any manifest path that is missing locally but exists in `.loa/` is counted as not-mounted, which never fails. A deleted link to a file the mount *does* link (a hook, say) is now indistinguishable from a path that is unlinked by design. Missing detection is effectively off in submodule mode.

6. `head/evals/tests/freeze.bats:38` and `:79` — `! grep ...` that is not the last command of a bats test can never fail the test, because `set -e` ignores negated commands. Reproduced with bats 1.13: `! true` followed by `echo ok` passes. The checks "every line is `<64hex>  tasks/`" and "no smoke/ entries without --smoke" are not enforced. Use `run ! grep` or `[ ... ]`.

7. `head/evals/tests/fixtures/mount-lib-stub.sh:24` — The stub emits `mount=whole_tree`, but the real library emits `mount=tree` (sandbox-mount.sh:134; arm-toggles.bats:326 asserts `mount=tree`). `pipeline-run.bats:245` asserts `whole_tree`, so it encodes a value the real pipeline never produces. Other divergences from the real contract:
   - `effort_stripped` vs `effort_skills_stripped`.
   - `resolve_arm_toggles` reads `.arms[]` only and has no `baseline → {}`.
   - `write_sandbox_grimoire` ignores `sprint_plan: false`.
   - `check_fixture_path_rule` has no `-L` check.

8. `head/tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh:137` (body at 124-135) — `run_step` calls `overlay` inside `if ! "$@"`, which turns off `set -e` inside the function. A failing `mkdir`, `cp -P` or `git add -A` is ignored, and `git commit --allow-empty` then succeeds. A broken overlay is never reported as exit 3, as the header promises.

9. `head/tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh:81` with `:153` — With a relative `--tmp` (or relative `TMPDIR`), `WORK` and `UP` are relative paths. `do_mount` changes into `$DOWN` first, so `bash "$UP/.claude/scripts/mount-submodule.sh"` resolves against the wrong directory, and `LOA_UPSTREAM="file://$UP"` is not a valid URL. The run fails with exit 3. `TMP_PARENT` is never made absolute.

10. `head/evals/harness/freeze.sh:69` — `find -type f` skips symlinks and does not descend into symlinked directories. Content reached through a symlink under `tasks/` (validate-suite.sh does not reject symlinks) is outside `MANIFEST.sha256`, so it can change with no drift reported.

11. `head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:383-386` — `regen_sandbox_manifest` runs `$EVAL_PROMPT_TREE/tools/gen-checksums.sh`, which is the PR tree's code. That script sources the prompt tree's `.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh` (gen-checksums.sh:51). This contradicts the header's trust-boundary rule (line 75: "never .claude/ code") whenever this branch is taken (the workspace is a git repo that tracks `.claude`).

12. `head/evals/harness/freeze.sh:43` — `--root` given as the last argument hits `shift 2` with one argument left; under `set -e` the script exits 1 with no message. Exit 1 means drift or validation failure here, not a usage error (2). Similarly `head/evals/harness/fingerprint.sh:44-46`: `${2:?...}` exits 1, but the header says usage errors are 2. Both reproduced.

13. Test hygiene:
    - `head/tests/unit/gen-checksums.bats:9` says the live manifest is "only read by GC-8", but there is no GC-8, so nothing checks the committed manifest's hashes.
    - `head/tests/unit/gen-checksums.bats:89` (GC-7) and `head/tests/unit/check-manifest-paths.bats:101` (MP-7) assume `BATS_TEST_TMPDIR` is outside any git work tree. Here `TMPDIR=/workspace/.eval/tmp` is inside the `/workspace` repo, and both tests fail.

One lower-confidence item, which only applies if the prompt tree's `.claude` contains symlinks pointing outside it: `head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:235` (`cat "$tmp" > "$f"`) and `:342` (`printf > "$mc.checksum"`) write through symlinks that `cp -a` keeps. The effort toggle would then edit the prompt tree's files instead of the sandbox copy, breaking the "SANDBOX COPY only" contract.

I could not run the freeze.bats cases (FZ-1 to FZ-6) or MP-6, because `grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0` is not in the PR snapshot. If that directory is not committed in the repo, FZ-6 will fail in CI.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.4, AC-1.3)
#
# Proves that a FRESH downstream submodule mount of this repository passes
# `check-loa.sh` integrity: no Tampered, no Missing (paths the mount does not
# link by design are reported as not-mounted and do not fail).
#
# Steps, all inside a new temp directory (nothing outside it is written):
#   1. upstream/   — a `git clone` of this repository over file://, with a
#                    local branch `fresh-mount-proof` at REF. With --worktree
#                    the source work tree's uncommitted state (tracked edits,
#                    deletions and untracked non-ignored files) is copied in
#                    and committed on that branch, inside the temp clone only.
#   2. downstream/ — `git init`, one commit, then the downstream entry point
#                    `upstream/.claude/scripts/mount-submodule.sh --branch
#                    fresh-mount-proof --ref <sha> --force` with
#                    LOA_UPSTREAM=file://.../upstream (the mount clones the
#                    submodule from there; no network).
#   3. `aleph.enabled: false` is set in downstream/.loa.config.yaml.
#   4. `bash .claude/scripts/check-loa.sh` runs in downstream/; its full output
#      is printed, then a summary line
#        fresh-mount-proof: Tampered=T Missing=M not-mounted=N check-loa-rc=R
#
# Git runs hermetically: GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1,
# a fixed identity, protocol.file.allow=always (needed for a file:// submodule
# on git >= 2.38.1) and core.hooksPath pointed at an empty directory.
#
# Usage:
#   tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh [--ref REF] [--worktree] [--keep] [--tmp DIR]

# --- 1. upstream clone ----------------------------------------------------------
UP="$WORK/upstream"
run_step "clone $SRC" git clone --quiet --no-checkout "file://$SRC" "$UP"
run_step "fetch $REF_SHA" git -C "$UP" fetch --quiet origin "$REF_SHA"
run_step "branch at $REF_SHA" git -C "$UP" checkout --quiet -B fresh-mount-proof "$REF_SHA"

overlay() {
  local p
  while IFS= read -r -d '' p; do
    if [[ -e "$SRC/$p" || -L "$SRC/$p" ]]; then
      [[ -d "$SRC/$p" && ! -L "$SRC/$p" ]] && continue   # gitlink / nested repo
      mkdir -p "$UP/$(dirname "$p")"
      rm -f "$UP/$p"
      cp -P "$SRC/$p" "$UP/$p"
    else
      rm -f "$UP/$p"
    fi
  done < <(git -C "$SRC" ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard)
  git -C "$UP" add -A
  git -C "$UP" commit --quiet --allow-empty -m "fresh-mount-proof: work-tree state of $SRC"
}
[[ $WORKTREE -eq 1 ]] && run_step "work-tree overlay" overlay
MOUNT_SHA="$(git -C "$UP" rev-parse HEAD)"
echo "fresh-mount-proof: mounting upstream commit $MOUNT_SHA"

# --- 2. downstream repository and the submodule mount --------------------------
DOWN="$WORK/downstream"
mkdir -p "$DOWN"
init_downstream() {
  git -C "$DOWN" init --quiet
  printf '# downstream fixture\n' > "$DOWN/README.md"
  git -C "$DOWN" add README.md
  git -C "$DOWN" commit --quiet -m "initial commit"
}
run_step "downstream init" init_downstream

do_mount() {
  (cd "$DOWN" && LOA_UPSTREAM="file://$UP" bash "$UP/.claude/scripts/mount-submodule.sh" \
    --branch fresh-mount-proof --ref "$MOUNT_SHA" --force < /dev/null)
}
run_step "mount-submodule.sh" do_mount
echo "fresh-mount-proof: mount-submodule.sh exited 0 ($(grep -c 'Linked' "$LOG" || true) link lines)"

# --- 3. Aleph off ---------------------------------------------------------------
CFG="$DOWN/.loa.config.yaml"

#       grimoires/loa/ledger.json (one active cycle, <sprint_label> planned, global 1;
#       the ledger-lib.sh schema), NOTES.md (header only), context/task-brief.md (the
#       task's agent-facing `criterion` + the TASK.md next to task.yaml),
#       a2a/<sprint_label>/ (empty); review-catch tasks also get a one-sprint
#       grimoires/loa/sprint.md naming pr/head.diff and a2a/<sprint_label>/reviewer.md
#       carrying pr/PR.md (sandbox copy, else the corpus fixture's). An arm whose
#       toggles carry sprint_plan: false (resolved from $LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE, default
#       evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml) gets NO sprint.md. Build tasks leave sprint.md
#       to the PLAN phase. Nothing written names the arm.
#   init_sandbox_beads <ws> <task_title>
#       `br init --prefix bd --no-daemon` in <ws> plus one task bead with the title
#       when br ($LOA_EVAL_BR_BIN, default br) is on PATH → beads=br; else the opt-out
#       marker through <ws>/.claude/scripts/beads/update-beads-state.sh --opt-out →
#       beads=opt-out; neither → beads=none (exit 0).
#
# Hashing is Python hashlib (_sm_sha256), never .claude/ code: see _sm_sha256.
# Callers source this file by a literal relative path (no variable expansion
# on the source line), as eval.yml's trust-boundary scan requires.
#
# Evidence: every function reports `key=value` lines (one line, no newline in
# the value). When ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE is set they are appended to that file;
# else they go to the descriptor in SANDBOX_MOUNT_EVIDENCE_FD (default 1).
# resolve_arm_toggles prints JSON on stdout and no evidence.
#
# Tested by evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats (directly and through execute-agent.sh)
# and evals/tests/execute-agent.bats.
# =============================================================================

[[ "${_SANDBOX_MOUNT_LOADED:-}" == "true" ]] && return 0
_SANDBOX_MOUNT_LOADED=true

_SM_LIB_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
_SM_REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$_SM_LIB_DIR/../../.." && pwd)"

_sm_err() { echo "ERROR: $*" >&2; }

# _sm_sha256 <file>... prints "<hex>  <file>" lines, the sha256sum output shape.
# Python hashlib, not compat-lib's sha256_portable: the eval workflow runs the
# harness as the trusted copy against a PR's .claude/, so no harness script
# sources .claude/ code (eval.yml "Validate grader trust boundary"); run-arms.sh
# hashes the corpus the same way.
_sm_sha256() {
  python3 -I -c '
import hashlib, sys
for p in sys.argv[1:]:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(p, "rb") as f:
        for b in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(b)
    print(h.hexdigest() + "  " + p)' "$@"
}

# _sm_evidence <key> <value> — one key=value line to the evidence sink.
_sm_evidence() {
  local line="$1=${2//$'\n'/ }"
  if [[ -n "${ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE:-}" ]]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE"
  else
    local fd="${SANDBOX_MOUNT_EVIDENCE_FD:-1}"
    [[ "$fd" =~ ^[0-9]$ ]] || fd=1
    printf '%s\n' "$line" >&"$fd"
  fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
mount_prompt_surface() {
  local ws="$1" tree="$2" skill="${3:-}"
  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "mount_prompt_surface: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
  [[ -d "$tree/.claude" ]] || { _sm_err "mount_prompt_surface: prompt tree has no .claude/: $tree"; return 2; }
  if [[ "$skill" == "-" ]]; then
    mkdir -p "$ws/.claude"
    cp -a "$tree/.claude/." "$ws/.claude/" || { _sm_err "mount_prompt_surface: copying .claude/ failed"; return 2; }
    printf '@.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md\n' > "$ws/CLAUDE.md"
    if [[ -f "$tree/.loa.config.yaml" ]]; then cp "$tree/.loa.config.yaml" "$ws/.loa.config.yaml"; fi
    _sm_evidence mount "tree"
    return 0
  fi
  case "$skill" in */*|.*|'') _sm_err "invalid skill name '$skill'"; return 2 ;; esac
  local skill_src="$tree/.claude/skills/$skill"
  [[ -f "$skill_src/SKILL.md" ]] || { _sm_err "prompt tree $tree has no .claude/skills/$skill/SKILL.md"; return 2; }
  mkdir -p "$ws/.claude/skills" "$ws/.claude/loa"
  # Whole skill dir (resources included) so guarded reads inside the skill resolve.
  local skill_dst="$ws/.claude/skills/$skill"
  mkdir -p "$skill_dst"
  cp -a "$skill_src/." "$skill_dst/"
  if [[ -f "$tree/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" ]]; then
    cp "$tree/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$ws/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
  fi
  if [[ -d "$tree/.claude/rules" ]]; then
    mkdir -p "$ws/.claude/rules"
    cp -a "$tree/.claude/rules/." "$ws/.claude/rules/"
  fi
  printf '@.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md\n' > "$ws/CLAUDE.md"
  if [[ -n "${LOA_EVAL_ARM+x}" && -f "$tree/.loa.config.yaml" ]]; then
    cp "$tree/.loa.config.yaml" "$ws/.loa.config.yaml"
  fi
  _sm_evidence mount "skill:$skill"
  return 0
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Dockerfile.ablation — container executor image for the cycle-130 component ablation
# (SDD D-4.9 / DEC-0411). Extends Dockerfile.sandbox's pinned base and non-root user
# with the Claude Code CLI, the codex CLI, pytest and bats. It holds NO credentials.
# pipeline-run.sh mounts exactly two host paths: the sandbox read-write at /workspace
# and a per-run writable HOME at /home/evaluser (<run>/meta/home: the codex CLI's
# auth.json/config.toml copies, empty .claude/ and .aws/; the CLI's session store). The
# Bedrock route authenticates from AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK passed in the environment.
# The image's tool versions (below) are the batch's versions: every arm runs here.
#
# Build (no build context is needed; nothing is COPY'd):
#   docker build -t loa-ablation:258 - < evals/harness/Dockerfile.ablation
# Run:
#   evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh --executor container --image loa-ablation:258 …
#   (pipeline-run.sh passes --rm --name --user --network bridge --read-only --tmpfs /tmp
#    --pids-limit 512 --memory 4g --cpus 2 and exactly the two mounts)
#
# Digest pinned 2026-02-11 (same base as Dockerfile.sandbox):
#   docker manifest inspect node:20.11.0-bookworm-slim | jq '.manifests[0].digest'
FROM rust:1-bookworm AS brbuild
RUN cargo install beads_rust --version 0.2.6 --root /opt/br --locked 2>/dev/null || cargo install beads_rust --version 0.2.6 --root /opt/br

FROM node:20.11.0-bookworm-slim@sha256:8ea90c4f037cc3c2f566eb46c53eaac005129113487eda4090058fe554578104 AS base

ARG CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=2.1.299
ARG CODEX_VERSION=0.162.1
ARG PYTEST_VERSION=9.0.2
ARG BATS_VERSION=v1.13.0

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    bash \
    git \
    jq \
    python3 \
    python3-pip \
    python3-venv \
    grep \
    diffutils \
    coreutils \
    procps \
    ca-certificates \
    curl \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# yq (mikefarah/yq) with SHA256 integrity verification (as Dockerfile.sandbox)
ARG YQ_VERSION=v4.40.5
ARG YQ_SHA256_AMD64=0d6aaf1cf44a8d18fbc7ed0ef14f735a8df8d2e314c4cc0f0242d35c0a440c95
ARG YQ_SHA256_ARM64=9431f0fa39a0af03a152d7fe19a86e42e9ff28d503ed4a70598f9261ec944a97
RUN arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) && \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) yq_arch="amd64"; yq_sha256="${YQ_SHA256_AMD64}" ;; \
      arm64) yq_arch="arm64"; yq_sha256="${YQ_SHA256_ARM64}" ;; \
      *) echo "Unsupported architecture: $arch" && exit 1 ;; \
    esac && \
    curl -fsSL "https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/${YQ_VERSION}/yq_linux_${yq_arch}" \
      -o /usr/local/bin/yq && \
    echo "${yq_sha256}  /usr/local/bin/yq" | sha256sum -c - && \
    chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq

# The two CLIs at the versions the fingerprint pins (exact versions, no ranges).
RUN npm install -g --no-fund --no-audit \
      "@anthropic-ai/claude-code@${CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION}" \
      "@openai/codex@${CODEX_VERSION}" \
    && npm cache clean --force

# pytest for Python fixtures (bookworm's pip is externally managed)
RUN pip3 install --no-cache-dir --break-system-packages "pytest==${PYTEST_VERSION}"
# cheval's declared dependencies (.claude/adapters/pyproject.toml: dependencies + the `full` extra),
# so the sandbox gates (adversarial-review.sh, flatline-orchestrator.sh) can dispatch (lead, DEC-0482)
RUN pip3 install --no-cache-dir --break-system-packages "rfc8785>=0.1.4" "jsonschema>=4.21" "pyyaml>=6.0" "httpx[http2]>=0.24.0"

# bats-core at the pinned tag
RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch "${BATS_VERSION}" https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core.git /tmp/bats-core && \
    /tmp/bats-core/install.sh /usr/local && \
    rm -rf /tmp/bats-core

# Disable npm lifecycle scripts for anything the agent installs later
RUN npm config set ignore-scripts true

# Non-root user (as Dockerfile.sandbox). At run time /home/evaluser is replaced by the
# per-run HOME bind mount and the process runs as the host uid (--user).
RUN groupadd -r evaluser && useradd -r -g evaluser -d /home/evaluser -s /bin/bash evaluser
# No beads (br) in the image: beads_rust 0.2.6 is not on crates.io and the host binary needs glibc 2.38+; the sandbox
# materialiser writes the beads opt-out marker (LOA_EVAL_BR_BIN unset/absent), so every arm runs the skills'
# markdown fallback alike (lead, Sprint 258).
RUN mkdir -p /home/evaluser/.aws /home/evaluser/.claude /home/evaluser/.codex /workspace && \
    chown -R evaluser:evaluser /home/evaluser /workspace

ENV TZ=UTC
ENV LC_ALL=C
ENV HOME=/home/evaluser
ENV NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=true
ENV CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1

USER evaluser
WORKDIR /workspace

# Health check — every tool the fingerprint names is present
RUN bash --version && git --version && jq --version && node --version && \
    python3 --version && python3 -m pytest --version && yq --version && \
    bats --version && claude --version && codex --version && \
    echo "All tools verified"

ENTRYPOINT []
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

"""cycle-125 Sprint 4 (PRD FR-5 AC 1–2, SDD §1.6) — the pricing resolution
ladder over the ids the fleet actually invokes (usage mining F5): dated
OpenAI releases, aliases, CLI-hop names. Each resolves through exact → dated
→ alias → hop with the rung recorded; unknown ids stay `unknown` and are
counted; ledger rows carry `pricing_resolution`, `resolved_model`,
`transport` and `cost_estimated`.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
import yaml

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

from loa_cheval.metering.ledger import create_ledger_entry  # noqa: E402
from loa_cheval.metering.pricing import find_pricing  # noqa: E402

CATALOG = ROOT.parents[1] / ".claude" / "defaults" / "model-config.yaml"

# The fleet ids from grimoires/loa/reports/usage-mining-2026-09-23.md §F5,
# with the rung each one must resolve through against the real catalog.
FLEET_IDS = [
    ("openai", "gpt-5.5-2026-04-23", "dated", "gpt-5.5"),
    ("openai", "gpt-5.2-2025-12-11", "dated", "gpt-5.2"),
    ("google", "gemini-2.5-pro", "exact", "gemini-2.5-pro"),
    ("openai", "codex-headless", "hop", "gpt-5.5"),
    ("anthropic", "claude-headless", "hop", "claude-fable-5-1"),
    ("anthropic", "claude-fable-5-1", "exact", "claude-fable-5-1"),
    ("anthropic", "fable", "alias", "claude-fable-5-1"),
    ("openai", "gpt-5.5-pro", "exact", "gpt-5.5-pro"),
]


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def catalog() -> dict:
    with CATALOG.open() as fh:
        return yaml.safe_load(fh)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("provider,model,rung,priced_as", FLEET_IDS)
def test_fleet_ids_resolve_with_the_expected_rung(catalog, provider, model, rung, priced_as):
    entry = find_pricing(provider, model, catalog)
    assert entry is not None, f"{provider}:{model} did not resolve"
    assert entry.resolution == rung
    assert entry.model == priced_as
    assert entry.input_per_mtok > 0


def test_unknown_ids_stay_unknown(catalog):
    assert find_pricing("openai", "totally-unknown-model", catalog) is None
    assert find_pricing("nobody", "zzz-unknown-9000", catalog) is None
    assert find_pricing("openai", "", catalog) is None
    # an alias requested under the wrong provider still prices (the alias's provider wins)
    assert find_pricing("nobody", "gpt-5.5", catalog).resolution == "alias"

content.text:
I found 11 likely defects in my scope; the first three hit the run's exit status or the cost cap. I ran `pipeline-run.bats` on a scratch copy in `/home/evaluser/prrev`, because `/tmp` here is mounted noexec.
- **With jq 1.7.1:** the 47 host-mode tests pass. The 5 container tests fail, but only because of the docker-stub path bug in item 10.
- **With the system jq 1.6:** almost every run fails (item 3).

### Findings, most severe first

1. `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:857-862` — **Infrastructure failures are scored as the agent's fault.**
   - A container-mode phase that never really started gets status `agent_error`, exit 1. That covers `docker run` failing (exit 125, e.g. the daemon is down) and the claude CLI, `python3` or `timeout` missing in the image (126/127).
   - The header (lines 98-100) promises exit 2 for "CLI/docker or image missing". In container mode nothing checks the CLI inside the image up front (only host mode, line 426).
   - The suite's exclusion rules don't drop `agent_error`, so these runs count as failed trials for the arm.

2. `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:586-588` (used at 731) — **The cost watchdog can silently switch off.**
   - Any failure of the pricing lookup yields `prices=null`, the in-phase watchdog is skipped, and the only trace is `watchdog.priced=false`.
   - The `cd .claude/adapters` doesn't help: under `python3 -I` neither the working directory nor the script's directory is on `sys.path` (I confirmed this with Python 3.11). So if `pricing.py` imports `loa_cheval`, it fails every time.
   - The tests never exercise this path, because they always set `LOA_EVAL_PRICING_JSON`.
   - With the watchdog off, the $12 cap is only checked after each phase, so a single phase (BARE allows 170 turns / 70 min) can overshoot it without limit.
   - It also runs `.claude/` code, which the header (lines 125-126) says the harness never does.
   - Caveat: `pricing.py` isn't in the PR, so I couldn't confirm it has an `--alias … --json` CLI or what it imports.

3. `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:224-225, 702-710, 816-826, 881-882` — **The script needs jq 1.7 but never checks (line 167 only checks that jq exists).** jq 1.6 is the Debian 12 / Ubuntu 22.04 default, and it is what this host has and what `Dockerfile.ablation` installs.
   - `label` is a reserved word in jq 1.6, so these jq programs don't compile and every phase dies with exit 2 (verified).
   - Separately, `split("\u0000") | .[:-1]` at 704-707 drops the last real element on jq 1.6. In my tests that silently removed the `--effort` value and `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false` from the recorded argv/env.

4. `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:489` — **Beads setup can contradict the container image.**
   - `init_sandbox_beads` runs on the host, and the library uses the host's `br` whenever it is on PATH.
   - The image ships no `br`, yet `Dockerfile.ablation:82-84` says the sandbox always gets the opt-out marker. Hosts with `br` installed will produce `br`-initialised sandboxes that the container can't use.

5. `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:246-250` — **A0's BARE caps stop matching the other arms when a task sets its own limits.**
   - The "BARE = PLAN + IMPLEMENT + 2×FIX" sum applies only when the suite doesn't declare BARE. The shipped suite declares BARE as 170 turns / 70 min.
   - So a task's per-phase limits (`bounds`, which every task must carry) reach A1's phases but never A0. That breaks the suite's stated "A0's BARE caps are PLAN + IMPLEMENT + 2 x FIX".

6. `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:595` vs `718` — **The price cache never works.** `price_for` runs inside `$(...)`, so the `PRICE_CACHE` update is lost. Pricing is fetched every phase, not "once per model" as line 91 says.

7. `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:431` vs `696` — **The recorded image may not be the image that ran.** `image_digest` is resolved once, but every phase runs `docker run` by tag. If the tag is rebuilt mid-batch, the recorded digest is wrong, contradicting line 86 ("image_digest identifies the batch's versions").

8. `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:713, 715, 772` — **The driver can abort and lose the phase record.**
   - These `wc -l < "$WS/.eval/…"` pipelines aren't guarded. If the agent removes `.eval/` (e.g. `git clean -fdx`; `.eval/` is only excluded via `.git/info/exclude`), `set -e` aborts the driver.
   - The result is `infrastructure_error` "driver aborted", with that phase's record and spend never written.

9. **Header/docs don't match the code.**
   - `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:85` says codex 0.137.0; `Dockerfile.ablation:25` pins 0.162.1.
   - `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:50` documents `index.json` keys as `IMPLEMENT|FIX1|FIX2`; line 788 lowercases them, and `ablation-row.sh` and the tests use lowercase.

10. `head/evals/tests/fixtures/docker-stub.sh:63` — **The docker stub maps paths wrongly.** `map()` replaces `/workspace` and `/home/evaluser` anywhere in a string, not just as a prefix. Host paths containing either string get corrupted. All 5 container tests fail when the bats temp dir is under `/home/evaluser` (reproduced), and would also fail under this environment's default `TMPDIR=/workspace/.eval/tmp`.

11. **Weak tests and a dead Docker stage.**
    - `head/evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats:602` vs `605`: the CHANGES_REQUIRED setup is wiped by `: > "$T/stub.env"` before every run. FIX phases never execute, so the "arm id never in snapshots/transcripts" check never covers FIX output.
    - `head/evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats:157`: an arithmetic tautology that can't fail.
    - `head/evals/harness/Dockerfile.ablation:19-20`: the `brbuild` stage is never used, and by the file's own comment (line 82) beads_rust 0.2.6 isn't on crates.io. BuildKit skips the stage, but the legacy builder (`DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0`) fails the build.

`execute-agent.sh` (compared against base) and the phase prompts showed no defects beyond those above. Nothing under `/workspace/pr/` was modified.

jq -r --arg n "$1" --arg d "$(builtin_model "$1")" --argjson o "$PHASE_MODELS_JSON" \
    '$o[$n] // .phase_defaults.models[$n] // $d' <<<"$SUITE_JSON"
}
phase_cap() {  # phase_cap <name> max_turns|timeout_min — task bounds > suite phase_defaults > built-in;
               # BARE without a declaration = PLAN + IMPLEMENT + 2 × FIX
  local n="$1" key="$2" v
  v="$(jq -r --arg n "$n" --arg k "$key" '.bounds[$k][$n] // empty' <<<"$TASK_JSON")"
  [[ -n "$v" ]] || v="$(jq -r --arg n "$n" --arg k "$key" '.phase_defaults[$k][$n] // empty' <<<"$SUITE_JSON")"
  if [[ -z "$v" && "$n" == "BARE" ]]; then
    v=$(( $(phase_cap PLAN "$key") + $(phase_cap IMPLEMENT "$key") + 2 * $(phase_cap FIX "$key") ))
  fi
  if [[ -z "$v" ]]; then
    if [[ "$key" == max_turns ]]; then v="$(builtin_turns "$n")"; else v="$(builtin_tmin "$n")"; fi
---
price_for() {  # price_for <model id> → {"in":…,"out":…,"cr":…,"cc":…} micro-USD per Mtok, or null
  local m="$1" hit alias j
  hit="$(printf '%s\n' "$PRICE_CACHE" | awk -F'\t' -v m="$m" '$1 == m {print $2; exit}')"
  [[ -n "$hit" ]] && { printf '%s' "$hit"; return 0; }
  if [[ -n "${LOA_EVAL_PRICING_JSON:-}" ]]; then
    j="$(jq -c --arg m "$m" '.[$m] // null' <<<"$LOA_EVAL_PRICING_JSON" 2>/dev/null || echo null)"
  else
    alias="$(printf '%s' "$m" | sed -E 's/^([a-z]+\.)?anthropic\.//; s/-v[0-9]+(:[0-9]+)?$//')"
    j="$(cd "$REPO_ROOT/.claude/adapters" && python3 -I "$REPO_ROOT/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/metering/pricing.py" \
          --alias "$alias" --json 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1p' || true)"
    [[ -n "$j" ]] || j=null
  fi
  j="$(jq -c 'if (type == "object") and (.input_per_mtok != null) and (.output_per_mtok != null)
              then {in: .input_per_mtok, out: .output_per_mtok,
                    cr: (.cache_read_per_mtok // (.input_per_mtok * 0.1)),
                    cc: (.cache_write_per_mtok // .cache_creation_per_mtok // (.input_per_mtok * 1.25))}
              else null end' <<<"$j" 2>/dev/null || echo null)"
  PRICE_CACHE="$PRICE_CACHE$m"$'\t'"$j"$'\n'
  printf '%s' "$j"
}
# price_events <events> <prices> <budget_micro> → "<turns> <estimate_micro> <crossing_turn|0>"
price_events() {
  jq -R -n -r --argjson p "$2" --argjson budget "$3" '
---
  local minv_before minv_after
  minv_before="$(wc -l < "$WS/.eval/model-invoke.jsonl" | tr -d ' ')"
  started_iso="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
  start_s="$(now_ms)"
  prices="$(price_for "$model")"
  budget=$(( CAP_MICRO - SPENT_MICRO ))
  CUR_LABEL="$label" CUR_CONTAINER="$cname"
  # the allowlist values enter the launcher's environment by export (never argv); the
  # shim then keeps exactly the allowlist (host) or the docker client's keys (container)
  ( cd "$WS" || exit 2
    if [[ "$EXECUTOR" == host ]]; then for kv in "${envkv[@]}"; do export "$kv"; done; fi
    exec "${full[@]}" ) < /dev/null > "$events" 2> "$errf" &
  CUR_PID=$!
  local poll="${LOA_EVAL_WATCHDOG_POLL_S:-1}"
  while kill -0 "$CUR_PID" 2>/dev/null; do
    sleep "$poll" || true
    [[ "$INTERRUPTED" -eq 1 ]] && break
    if [[ "$prices" != null ]]; then
      est="$(price_events "$events" "$prices" "$budget")"
      if [[ "${est##* }" -gt 0 ]]; then
        killed=1; cap_turn="${est##* }"
        echo "pipeline-run.sh: watchdog: $label estimate passes the cap at turn $cap_turn; SIGTERM" >&2

     snapshot: (if $snap == "" then null else $snap end),
     verdict: (if $verdict == "null" or $verdict == "" then null else $verdict end),
     watchdog: {priced: ($priced != "null"), estimate_usd: ($est_micro / 1000000), turns_seen: $est_turns,
                killed: ($killed == 1), cap_turn: (if $killed == 1 then $cap_turn else null end)},
     started: $started, finished: $finished}' >> "$PHASES_FILE"

  # --- account and decide ---
  local cost_micro
  cost_micro="$(jq -r --argjson e "${est_micro:-0}" '(.total_cost_usd // ($e / 1000000)) * 1000000 | round' <<<"$result")"
  SPENT_MICRO=$(( SPENT_MICRO + cost_micro + ledger_micro ))
  if [[ "$INTERRUPTED" -eq 1 ]]; then finish interrupted 4 "driver received a signal during $label"; fi
  if [[ "$killed" -eq 1 ]]; then CAP_PHASE="$label"; CAP_TURN="$cap_turn"; finish cap_failure 3 "watchdog stopped $label at turn $cap_turn"; fi
  if [[ "$timed_out" == false ]] && { [[ $rc -eq 143 ]] || [[ $rc -eq 137 ]] || [[ $rc -eq 129 ]] || [[ $rc -eq 130 ]]; }; then
    finish interrupted 4 "phase $label was killed from outside (exit $rc)"
  fi
  if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then
    if [[ "$timed_out" == true ]]; then finish agent_error 1 "phase $label timed out after ${tsec}s"; fi
    finish agent_error 1 "phase $label exited $rc"
  fi
  if [[ $SPENT_MICRO -ge $CAP_MICRO ]]; then
    CAP_PHASE="$label"; finish cap_failure 3 "spend USD $(jq -n --argjson s "$SPENT_MICRO" '$s/1000000') reached the cap USD $MAX_RUN_USD after $label"
  fi

head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:266 — integrity_clean never compares the sandbox checksums.json against arm_evidence.manifest_sha256 recorded at mount time; a mismatch only drops the "(matches checksums.json)" suffix from the evidence. The manifest lives in the agent-writable sandbox, so an agent that edits .claude/ files and regenerates (or prunes) checksums.json passes the rule: the integrity proof checks the tree against itself. Fail when "$filesha" != "$msha".
head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:386 — regen_sandbox_manifest executes "$EVAL_PROMPT_TREE/tools/gen-checksums.sh", which is the code of the PR/source tree under evaluation, and that script sources the same tree's .claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh (tools/gen-checksums.sh:51). The trusted harness therefore runs PR-controlled code, against this library's own trust-boundary rule (line 75: "never .claude/ code"; eval.yml "Validate grader trust boundary"). Use the inline hashlib path always, or the harness's own copy of the tool.
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:586 — pricing runs the evaluated tree's .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/metering/pricing.py, which also crosses the trust boundary (header lines 125-126). Any failure (missing CLI flag, import error under python3 -I, where neither the cwd nor the script dir is on sys.path for package imports) yields prices=null. That silently turns off the in-phase watchdog (line 731 is skipped) and leaves only the post-phase check (line 864), so one phase (BARE: 170 turns / 70 min) can overrun the USD 12 per-run cap without limit. The only trace is watchdog.priced=false. With no price, fail closed (infrastructure_error) instead.
head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:563 — --run-cap only reserves headroom per in-flight trial. Nothing passes the cap to the trial (run_trial / execute-agent have no budget flag), so a trial can cost more than run_cap and --max-usd is overshot even though the gate "reserved" for it. The header's "run_cap … reserved per running trial" promise is not enforced.
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:702 — jq programs bind `--arg label` / `$label` (lines 702/708, 816/826, 881/882), and ablation-row.sh:285 uses the `{name, label, …}` shorthand. `label` is a reserved word in jq 1.6, so these fail to compile ("unexpected label") and every phase dies on jq 1.6, the Debian 12 / Ubuntu 22.04 default. Line 167 only checks that jq exists, not its version. Also on jq 1.6, the NUL split at 704-707 (`split("\u0000") | .[:-1]`) drops argv/env elements, which silently loses the --effort/--resume values and LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false from the capture that took-effect.sh reads (reproduced: took-effect FAILs A4/A6/A7 on jq 1.6). Either rename the variable and key or require and check jq >= 1.7.
head/evals/tests/ablation-row.bats:19 — setup copies "$FX/runs", but evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/runs/ is not in the change: the whole ablation-runs/ directory is new and regen.sh writes runs/ for the tracked tree, yet no runs/ file is in the diff. Every ablation-row.bats test (and took-effect.bats:18) fails at setup, and the new CI step (.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:221) runs evals/tests/, so CI goes red. Commit the regenerated runs/.
head/evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats:610 — `! grep -rqF "$arm" …` is not the last command, and bats' set -e ignores negated commands, so the meta-boundary assertion (arm id never in sandbox/snapshots/transcripts/eval) can never fail. The same inert pattern guards the secret and leak checks at 237, 332, 339, 391-394, 652, 668 and 726. Also, line 609 resets stub.env with `: >`, so the CHANGES_REQUIRED setup at line 605 is dead and no FIX output is ever checked. Use `run ! grep` or `if grep …; then false; fi`.
head/evals/tests/freeze.bats:38 — `! grep -qv '^[0-9a-f]\{64\}  tasks/'` (and line 79, `! grep -q '  smoke/'`) is not the last command of its test, so it can never fail: the manifest line-format and the smoke-exclusion assertions are not enforced.
head/tools/check-manifest-paths.sh:80 — `git ls-files -- .claude` runs without -z, so with the default core.quotePath git C-quotes non-ASCII or quote-bearing names (".claude/caf\303\251.sh"), while the manifest keys from jq (line 81) are raw UTF-8. A correct manifest from gen-checksums.sh (which uses -z and accepts such names) is reported as having untracked paths, and the new CI gate fails. Use `ls-files -z` and NUL-aware comparison, or `-c core.quotePath=false`.
head/.claude/scripts/preflight.sh:190 — the integrity count now comes from `git ls-files` (the index), not the files on disk. Deleting a tracked System Zone file, or dropping a stray file into .claude/, no longer changes ACTUAL_COUNT, so the "modified outside the update process" warning cannot fire for those cases. A downstream that commits .claude/ but whose manifest was written by the legacy find-based generators (mount-loa.sh/update.sh) now gets a false mismatch (exit 1 under strict).
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:862 — any non-zero phase exit that is not a timeout or a signal is classed agent_error (exit 1): `docker run` failing (125), and the CLI, python3 or timeout missing in the image (126/127). The header (lines 98-100) promises exit 2 / infrastructure for "CLI/docker or image missing", and container mode never checks the in-image CLI up front. These infrastructure faults are scored as failed trials (agent_error is not in the suite's exclusion statuses).
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:248 — the BARE "PLAN + IMPLEMENT + 2 × FIX" sum applies only when nothing declares BARE, and the shipped suite declares BARE: 170/70 (ablation-2.0.yaml:50-51). A task's own bounds for PLAN/IMPLEMENT/FIX therefore tighten A1's phases but never A0's BARE session, which breaks the comparable-budget premise the suite file states (line 39).
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:718 — `prices="$(price_for "$model")"` runs price_for in a subshell, so its PRICE_CACHE update (line 595) is lost and pricing is recomputed (running pricing.py) for every phase, contrary to "fetched once per model" (line 91).
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:713 — the unguarded `wc -l < "$WS/.eval/cost-ledger.jsonl"` / model-invoke reads (also 715 and 772) run on agent-writable files. If the agent removes .eval/ (e.g. `git clean -fdx`), set -e aborts the driver, and the phase record and its spend are never written. The run reads infrastructure_error with spend under-counted.
head/tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh:133 — the --worktree overlay walks only `ls-files --cached --others`. A file removed with `git rm` (or the old path of a `git mv`) is no longer in the index, so it is never deleted from the upstream clone, although the header (lines 11-13) says deletions are applied. The proof can then pass on a tree that still holds removed files.
head/tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh:137 — run_step calls overlay inside `if ! "$@"`, which disables set -e within the function. A failing mkdir/cp -P/git add -A is ignored and `git commit --allow-empty` still succeeds, so a broken overlay is never reported as exit 3.
head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:144 — in skill mode the cp -a of the skill dir (144), the cp of CLAUDE.loa.md (146), the rules copy (150) and the config copy (154) are unchecked. Callers invoke the function under `|| exit 2` or `$(…) || rc=$?`, which suspends set -e, so a failed copy returns 0 and the arm runs on an incomplete prompt surface. The base execute-agent ran these copies at top level, where set -e aborted.
head/evals/tests/fixtures/mount-lib-stub.sh:24 — the stub emits mount=whole_tree, but the real library emits mount=tree (lib/sandbox-mount.sh:134, asserted by arm-toggles.bats:326). pipeline-run.bats:245 thus pins a value the real pipeline never produces, and any consumer written against the fixtures will mis-handle real runs.
